bindings.reason: DEVIATION FROM THE LITERAL SKETCH SPAN, BY ORCHESTRATOR RULING. op_copy_out is realized at the HOST boundary, not by a Triton store: `destination.copy_(self.out_ws)` in _direct_serve / _copyin_serve. The sketch declares `writes: [out_dest]` (a two-hop out_ws -> out_dest -> fresh), but the shipped C3 form copies out_ws DIRECTLY into the fresh per-call tensor, in ONE copy, and out_dest is NOT written on the served path. Ruling: the literal span was predicated on the now-falsified premise that persisting the copy destination pays for itself; the two-hop measured +5.113 us/call (p15 C2) while C3 measures -0.022 us (p15 C3), so the literal is formalism over evidence and is OVERRIDDEN. The sketch's INTENT -- out_ws (graph-pool) is never returned, and the returned tensor never aliases across calls -- is fully satisfied by C3. The recorded span is the device store producing the out_ws contents the host copy then moves into the fresh tensor.

bindings.notes: THIS IS THE NON-ALIASING GUARANTEE. forward() returns a FRESH tensor per call, never out_dest and never a view of it, so a tensor the caller retains is never overwritten. Verified by the retention test over 50 further forwards using the p12 CHANGING-DATA protocol (p10 R1) and by the no-alias census (p10 R2). In C3 the sketch's two declared hops collapse into this single step plus the direct copy in op_copy_out.
